M1_S01.summary: Aññasamāna means 'common to the other': the group holds seven universals and six occasionals, all taking their moral quality from the citta they accompany.
body: Aññasamāna: añña means 'another', samāna means 'common' — hence 'common to the other'. These factors resemble whatever they accompany: as the other is, so are they.

M1_S02.summary: Contact is the meeting of consciousness with its object, and feeling is the experiencing of that object — contact being the nutriment on which feeling depends.

M1_S03.summary: Perception recognises an object by the mark it has noted, while volition, the most important factor, organises the others and is itself what makes kamma.

M1_S04.summary: One-pointedness gathers the mind onto a single object, the life faculty maintains the mental states, and attention turns the mind towards its object.
